title: Decommissioning and recycling safety assumptions for the hypothetical 400 V BMS

standards_mappings.reference: Part 7, Clause 12 (end of life and decommissioning)
standards_mappings.rationale: The end-of-life activity this record identifies.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('the end-of-life activity this record identifies'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic and belongs to the hypothetical Project Northcell. No organisation, plant, vehicle, technician or recycler named here exists.
purpose: State what this item assumes about its own end of life, who is responsible for what, and what control makes each assumption visible. An item that assumes nothing is an item whose end-of-life obligations have been pushed onto a party that never agreed to them.

What the item assumes about the state of the pack at that point

procedures.action: The item assumes it is removed from a vehicle by a qualified party and that the vehicle's high-voltage system has been isolated by the vehicle's own means before removal
procedures.acceptance_condition: The assumption is stated to every party that performs a removal, including the recycler
procedures.decision_point: Whether removal may be performed by an unqualified party

procedures.action: The item assumes that at removal the pack may still be energised and may still be within its operating envelope, and that this is not knowable from the item after removal
procedures.acceptance_condition: No procedure relies on the item being able to report its own state at removal; the assumption is that it cannot

procedures.action: The item contributes a final state record: its configuration identification, its event log and its diagnosis state, written to non-volatile memory and readable after removal
procedures.acceptance_condition: The final state record is written before removal and remains readable after it
procedures.decision_point: Whether an item whose final state cannot be written is removed at all

procedures.action: The item declares that it contributes nothing to end-of-life safety once removed, and that the responsibility for a removed pack lies with the party handling it
procedures.acceptance_condition: The declaration appears in the service documentation the removing party receives, not only here
procedures.decision_point: This step is a declaration and carries no decision point; no synthetic_decision label applies

procedures.action: The item assumes the receiving party treats a removed pack as energised until a measurement says otherwise, and that it can reach that measurement
procedures.acceptance_condition: The assumption is recorded here and passed to the receiver in the service documentation; it is not enforced by anything in the item

records_produced.retention: retained until the pack is recycled

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The pack is removed from a vehicle by a party qualified to work on a 400 volt system, with the vehicle's high-voltage system isolated by the vehicle first.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. No party has agreed it and nothing enforces it.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A person works on an energised pack. This is the assumption whose failure is fatal rather than merely inconvenient, which is why it is first and why no control in this item can be relied upon to catch it.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The service documentation states the assumption at the point of removal, not in a decommissioning record the removing party never sees.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: At removal the pack may be energised and within its operating envelope, and its state cannot be determined from the item after removal.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Derived from the chemistry: a lithium-ion cell retains a hazardous voltage long after load is removed. The item cannot measure its own state once disconnected.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A removed pack is treated as safe because the item recorded a normal state before removal, and is handled accordingly while still holding a hazardous charge.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The final state record states that it describes the item's state at removal and is not a statement about the pack's charge.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The receiving party can reach a measurement of the removed pack's voltage before it does anything else.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. It depends on the receiving party's equipment and training, neither of which this project controls.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: The receiving party acts before measuring. Nothing in the item prevents this and nothing in this corpus addresses it.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The receiver assumption record passed with the service documentation. The control is communication, not enforcement, and it is recorded as such.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The cell chemistry's own end-of-life requirements are met by the cell supplier and are not the item's to discharge.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared and consistent with the item definition's scope statement, which places thermal runaway and cell chemistry outside the item's boundary.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: A cell is treated as a component rather than as a hazardous material at end of life, and the item's boundary was wrong in a way that matters at exactly one moment in the product's life.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: The scope statement in FB2-SAF-ITE-000001 classifies the hazard as inherent to the chemistry rather than to the item, so the boundary decision is visible and can be challenged.

end_of_life_assumptions.assumption: The item is not modified after removal in a way that a removing party would reasonably expect to be safe.
end_of_life_assumptions.basis: Declared. Not enforceable by the item.
end_of_life_assumptions.if_false: The item is opened or its contacts bridged, and a stored charge discharges through an unintended path.
end_of_life_assumptions.control_that_makes_it_visible: None. This record states the assumption and states that no control exists, which is the honest position and is the reason the assumption appears here at all.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The removal assumptions are delivered in the service documentation at the point of removal
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: The assumptions exist in a record the removing party never sees, which is the same as them not existing.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The final state record carries the configuration identification
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A pack's remaining life cannot be estimated from the record left behind.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The field record informs the end-of-life decision
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A pack is retired for a reason its own record contradicts, or kept because a record is missing.

operational_authorisation_statement: This record is a fictional engineering artefact. It is NOT an authorised decommissioning procedure, it instructs nobody to dismantle anything, and no pack, item or recycler exists. production_authorized is false.

evidence_state.reason: No production line, vehicle, charging site, workshop, fleet or recycling facility exists anywhere in this corpus. Master-prompt clause 2.5 forbids energising hardware and connecting to vehicles, so no step below can be performed by any means available here. The record documents the procedure and records that it has not been run.

limitations: Synthetic. There is no pack, no item, no vehicle and no recycler. Nothing below has been performed and no assumption below has been agreed by any party.

No regulatory requirement on battery end-of-life or waste handling is stated or assessed anywhere in this record. That is a real omission: a real programme's decommissioning record would be dominated by such requirements, and this one cannot be, because this corpus neither knows nor asserts them.
The first assumption is the one whose failure is fatal, and the item has no control over it. The record says so rather than listing a control it does not have.

One assumption is recorded explicitly with 'control_that_makes_it_visible: none'. An assumption with no control is still worth recording, because a programme that does not record it will discover it in the field.
This record contributes nothing to end-of-life safety in practice. Its value is that it says explicitly who owns the risk once the item is gone, rather than leaving the question open.
